official.rated_power_w: 200 W 'on the surface' - NASA NSSDC, Intuitive Machines 3 (Nova-C lander): 'It uses solar panels to generate 200 W of power on the surface.'
official.shape: 'a tall hexagonal cylinder on 6 landing legs' - same NSSDC entry
official.planned_surface_operations: 'Approximately 10 days' - NASA CLPS IM-2 press kit

seen_only_through_web_search.size: 4.0 m tall, 1.57 m wide (NSSDC entry for IM-1; the page returned an error when read directly)
seen_only_through_web_search.battery: 25 Ah at 28 V = 700 Wh (same NSSDC IM-1 entry, same caveat)

generic_assumptions.panel_placement: NOT published by NASA or Intuitive Machines in any page we could read. Three generic arrangements are modelled instead: six vertical panels on the faces, one horizontal panel, one Sun-tracking panel.
generic_assumptions.area_rule: Areas are scaled so that each arrangement gives the official 200 W in its best case: the tracking and horizontal panels at normal incidence, the six faces with the Sun on the horizon.
generic_assumptions.charge_curve: full acceptance (0.5 C) up to 80 % charge, linear taper to zero at 100 %; efficiency 0.95
generic_assumptions.yaw: upright lander: one face toward north; on its side: averaged over 12 fall directions
generic_assumptions.shading: only the horizon mask (visible fraction of the solar disk); panels shading each other, the ground under a fallen lander and dust are not modelled
